pezzi.1: What an AI agent really is: how it is built inside, the four parts it needs to hold up in service, and why companies are asking for one now.
pezzi.3: What an AI agent really is: how it is built inside, the four parts it needs to hold up in service, and why companies are asking for one now.
pezzi.4: Andrea Sforna AI: design, security and maintenance of AI agent systems
pezzi.6: What an AI agent really is: how it is built inside, the four parts it needs to hold up in service, and why companies are asking for one now.
pezzi.36: A model answers. An agent receives a goal, chooses which operations to call, checks the result and stops when it is done or when it cannot go on.
pezzi.38: They are three different things, and they are confused all the time. The difference is not how intelligent the model is: it is how much autonomy it has, and who set its boundaries.
pezzi.42: Answers, one question at a time
pezzi.46: It looks like an ordinary conversation. Underneath, every field is the result of a declared operation on the company database: no free-form search, no data recalled from memory.
pezzi.47: Find me the customer record for Rossi
pezzi.50: Here is the record of the customer found with “Rossi” (
pezzi.63: One result only. If you want the full details (overdue invoices, orders), tell me.
pezzi.64: No free-form search: the agent’s only action is the operation it was given, run with the requester’s permissions.
pezzi.65: How much did we spend on transport in the first half of the year?
pezzi.68: DATA MISSING · no “transport” line in the chart of accounts
pezzi.71: returns seven categories and none of them is transport: the spending may sit inside “logistics” or be recorded as general costs.
pezzi.75: Logistics, January–June 2026: 18.940 € across 62 documents. If you want, I can check which ones are actual transport and which are warehouse, but that means reading the individual entries.
pezzi.76: The moment that sets a serious system apart: declaring what isn’t there instead of producing a plausible number.
pezzi.78: The question is legitimate, the answer is not in the data. The agent says so, explains where it might be, and waits for an instruction instead of filling the gap.
pezzi.79: What it is for, and what it is not for
pezzi.80: The useful question is not whether an agent can do something, but whether that something is repetitive, verifiable and bounded.
pezzi.82: The work repeats and follows a recognisable rule
pezzi.83: The information sits in archives that can be reached
pezzi.84: There is a way to check that the result is right
pezzi.85: The task crosses several steps and several tools
pezzi.87: The decision needs a person to take responsibility
pezzi.88: The process does not exist yet, or changes every time
pezzi.89: There is no way to check the outcome
pezzi.90: The problem is solved by one well-written rule
pezzi.92: A serious agent is four things put together, and none of the four is the model. The model is the replaceable part.
pezzi.94: Declared operations, with an MCP server in front
pezzi.96: Permissions in the database and in the operating system
pezzi.98: Every statement traces back to a read
pezzi.101: Why it is being asked for now
pezzi.102: Three things changed in the same period, and together they make possible what would not have held up two years earlier. None of the three is about the intelligence of the model itself.
pezzi.104: They hold up on tasks with several steps
pezzi.106: Operations are declared instead of improvised
pezzi.110: An agent is not a more intelligent model. It is a model with boundaries.
pezzi.112: An agent does not remove the work of the person who decides. It moves it: from carrying things out to setting goals, scope and criteria for checking. If nobody does that part, the system does not hold up.
pezzi.115: An agent that publishes, an agent inside an application, a group of agents that check each other.
